html:
The Deesis mosaic is a large mosaic in the south gallery of Hagia Sophia in Constantinople. It shows Christ in the middle, with the Virgin Mary and John the Baptist on either side, turned towards him and pleading for mankind. Deesis is Greek for "prayer" or "supplication".

It is usually dated to around 1261, soon after the recovery of the city from the Latins, and may have been made to mark the return of Orthodox worship to the great church. Only the upper part survives, but the faces are among the finest works of Byzantine art, soft and tender, modelled with tiny tiles in subtle shades. Many see in them the start of the late Byzantine revival of the arts, seen later in the Chora church.

Like the other mosaics of Hagia Sophia, it was later covered over and was uncovered in the 1930s.
